scope: Two existing guide associations only, after reviewed source-link corrections.

decisions.label: Gather approved website facts
decisions.reason: The guide helps the recreation-business reader gather owner-approved facts for the separate boat and cabin offers: current reservation links, dates, arrival locations, confirmation responsibilities and the meaning of each inquiry. Its confirmed/needs-approval/not-available claim states are especially relevant now that the Messer example is explicitly historical. The brief still requires current owner-supplied instructions rather than treating archived booking arrangements as current policy.
guideEvidence: Gather the facts before polishing the words: mark each claim confirmed, needing approval or unavailable, and identify its approver.
Build a service page around fit and scope: explain what is needed first, the work sequence and the next responsible person.
Contact page: name the request and clarify human review before booking is confirmed.
decisions.boundary: The guide does not verify current Messer availability or combine two reservations. It helps prepare accurate present-day business facts for the proposed website.

decisions.label: Separate an equipment inspection request from approval to repair
decisions.reason: The guide remains a useful repair-process analogy for the strand-service brief: identify the particular piece, describe observed condition, preserve uncertain service history and explain when assessment becomes approved work. This directly supports the intact inherited strand and broken-strand scenarios, which leave diagnosis and suitable work to the jeweler. The narrower source claim that restringing is listed does not remove that proposed customer decision. The equipment-specific requirements are examples to adapt, not jewelry intake policies to copy.
guideEvidence: Describe the intake your business actually uses: name what the first request means, identify the item and record the observed problem.
Show the decision before the customer incurs it: a general request for help is not agreement to unspecified repair; assessment and authorization must be explained.
Sources and scope / preparation instructions: adapt actual approved policies and leave technical acceptance to responsible specialists.
decisions.boundary: This is an equipment-to-jewelry workflow analogy. RMA, purchase-order, industrial shipping and multi-unit policies are not asserted to apply to jewelry; the actual guide title in the link label makes its equipment focus visible.
